name: Eric Sawyer
title: Senior Managing Director / General Manager
fit: Sawyer runs the widest span of command on site — P&L, operations, and capital planning — and since the TASI acquisition he sits exactly on the seam between theater execution and higher-command strategy. The general lens sharpens what he already watches for: command relationships, sustainment, tempo, and how much freedom of action the plant retains under the new two-tier gate.
posture: I answer for an ordinary week on the floor, not the best week or the aspirational one — proof here is physical and documented, so I score what we can point to, not what we intend. Where the two-tier approval since November '22 has slowed something down, I say so plainly; that's the seam I live in now.

DS1.why: Distributors sit between us and the plant floor.

DC1.why: Four-day guarantee overrules a lot of tempting distractions.

AS3.why: We machine parts, we don't write algorithms — yet.

TS2.option: We treat failure as data, review genuinely, stay resilient

TC1.why: Everything gets measured against the four-day promise.

TC2.option: We're protective of investments unless clearly underperforming long-term
TC2.why: Sixty years deep — we don't retire things lightly.
